For each active cell, it performs QEF minimisation to determine the dual vertex position, using edge intersection points and finite-difference gradient normals, applying Tikhonov regularisation towards the mass point for rank-deficient cases.
The isovalue is typically a percentile (e.g., 90th) of the wind speed array.
A surface extraction method for volume fraction data stored on an octree.
Unlike Dual Contouring, this method does not require gradient vectors, making it suitable for volume fraction data where only scalar values are available.
-   **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of voxels, as each cell is processed once.
-   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ for storing the grid and dual vertices.
-   **When to Use:** When manifold geometry, smooth shading, and connectivity are required.
-   **When Not to Use:** When simple, fast triangle soup is sufficient, or when the grid is extremely sparse and hierarchical traversal overhead is prohibitive.
It was designed to address the topological ambiguities and non-manifold issues of standard Marching Cubes and Dual Contouring.
The method unifies MC surface fragments into polygonal patches, creating a dual surface that is always a topological manifold.
